email_check_2026_11_16.question: Can the backend send through the carpals.ir mailbox on cPanel (webmail Roundcube)?
email_check_2026_11_16.answer: Yes, through authenticated SMTP submission. Roundcube is only the webmail reader; the backend talks SMTP to the same mail server.
findings: DNS: MX carpals.ir -> mail.carpals.ir (89.44.243.175, the cPanel host; Exim 4.100.1 on s444.bitcommand.com). The API server api.carpals.ir is another machine (185.110.190.201), so it must reach mail.carpals.ir over the network.

Port 465 (implicit TLS): certificate valid for mail.carpals.ir (also carpals.ir, www.carpals.ir); offers AUTH PLAIN LOGIN. Port 587: STARTTLS, then AUTH. Both reachable from the owner's machine on 2026-11-16; reachability from the API server is still to be checked there (deploy.md command).

SPF "v=spf1 mx a:mailgw-c.getway.biz a:imailgw-c.getway.biz -all": mail sent through the cPanel server passes; mail sent directly from the API server's own IP would fail SPF (-all). So the backend must submit to mail.carpals.ir, never deliver mail itself.
DKIM: default._domainkey.carpals.ir is published (cPanel signs outgoing mail). DMARC: p=none (monitoring only); tighten to quarantine after the pilot shows clean reports.

Limits: the server answers LIMITS MAILMAX=1000 (per connection). The hosting plan's hourly sending cap is not visible from outside: the owner asks the host (shared hosting often allows a few hundred messages an hour). Enough for sign-in codes and notices in the pilot; review before marketing mail.
The banner says the system must not be used for unsolicited or bulk email: transactional mail only; marketing mail needs its own provider later.

Design decided in DQ-04 (2026-11-13): own recovery codes, requester proof (password + code + emailed code), two ADM approvals in the console with an out-of-band check, 72-hour restriction, break glass on the server. S16b: account recovery from the console sign-in (email, password or forgotten, one recovery code, emailed code; same answer whatever the account), two ADM approvals with a fresh aal3 and an out-of-band check, any ADM rejects, 24-hour expiry, completion with a new device-bound key (old keys, codes and sessions end, new codes once), 72-hour restriction (STAFF_RECOVERY_RESTRICTED).

scale.P0: Pilot blocker: a security or privacy defect, a legal obligation, or a state staff cannot get out of without SQL on the server.
scale.P1: Pilot operations: a pilot flow or a Docs/23 Must screen cannot be done in the console, or a server-side safety rule is missing; a console workaround may exist but is weak.
scale.P2: Completeness and efficiency: Docs/23 Should items, extra filters and context, aggregates; the console has a working workaround.
scale.P3: Tied to a later feature (the AI build).

complexity_scale.S: ~1 point: one read operation, or a field or filter on an existing operation.
complexity_scale.M: ~2-3 points: two or three operations, or one rule plus a scheduler job, or a new column with a migration.
complexity_scale.L: ~4-6 points: a new entity with its operations, or a rule that cuts across many operations.
complexity_scale.XL: 6+ points: a cross-module rewrite with per-module conflict rules.
complexity_scale.note: Points are relative effort per the backend definition of done (Docs/40 text, registry and codegen, handler, projection, sweep resolver, happy-path + authz-negative + rule tests). Reference: backend S12 (3 new operations, 2 changed, staff tooling, contract bump) is about 9 points.

method: Closed items (BR-01..BR-06) are kept for history only.
Each open item is rated by what goes wrong without it at the pilot, not by its source label (blocker/high/must/should): the source labels described when the console needed it.
Items whose parts differ in risk are split (BR-35 row vs filters vs more-info vs correction; BR-15 actions vs redaction; BR-21 list vs notification; BR-26 ids vs notice).
Console workarounds already built (deviations D-xx) lower the priority only when they are safe; they never lower a server-side safety or privacy rule.

findings: BR-35 part 1 is a privacy defect, not a missing feature: admin.orgs_search is not PURP but returns StaffOrgView rows with contact email, phone and exact points, while admin.org_get with the same view is PURP PII (DI-31). It is raised to P0 and fixed with BR-09.
BR-09 and BR-35 (1) together decide what staff can see without a justified purpose; both must be closed before real staff use real data (R-03).
BR-20 is small but P0: privacy requests have deadlines and the export cannot be shown or handed over from the console today (DI-14).
BR-32 is P1 although the console already offers only "high" in triage (D-57): AI flags and rules open cases without passing through the console, so only the server can enforce the floor.
BR-30 is a docs decision first; the console already shows the effect of each outcome (D-44), so it is not urgent.
BR-07 and BR-08 close backend DI-66 and DI-67 (backend NI-04). Backend DI-05 (assist routes) is the remaining NI-04 part and is out of scope (DI-08).
BR-14 depends on the AI build only for its value, not for its data: ai_mcp.ai_insights exists, so a review-decision table can be added now.

principles: Order: first the reads that unblock the console (S13), then the pilot blockers (privacy S14, legal S15, staff keys S16a/S16b), then pilot-operations completeness (S17-S19), then Should items (S20-S24), then the owner's carry-overs (S25a), then closure (S25b).

One stage = one working session that fits a 5-hour token window. Target load <= 11 points (backend S12 was about 9, S11 about 11). Security-sensitive or cross-module stages are planned lighter (S16a, S16b, S22, S23).

A stage groups items by module and contract area so the session reads one set of docs and code (backend conventions.context_budget: read only the listed ranges, lean on the generated registry, copy patterns from finished modules).

Every stage follows the backend definition of done per operation and ends with contract:check and openapi:check green and the console contract regenerated, so the tree is never left with a half-updated registry.
If a session runs long, stop at the stage's split_point and move the rest to S25b or the named later stage; never split inside a task.

Stage-level unit and integration tests in lite mode stay part of each stage (they are development, not the test run). The strict cross-component runs (console and PWA E2E and test:int, R-10, R-13, R-20) wait for the whole-plan test run after S25b (PD-03). DQ-08 asks the owner to confirm this reading.

deviations.deviation: A record outside the purpose item answers 403 PURPOSE_RECORD_MISMATCH (the stage text), not 404 NOT_FOUND as risk_control_plan RCP-01.A2 (2026-10-24) proposed. An item that is not open in the caller's queue still answers 404. No existence oracle: a record that does not exist and an unrelated one get the same 403, because the binding compares ids (or, for a file, finds no subject) before any handler reads the record.
deviations.impact: The console can tell "wrong work item" from "not found" (kit message added). RCP-01.A2 is closed with this wording.

deviations.deviation: admin.users_search is not refused under an unrelated purpose: a search has no single record, so it finds only the users the purpose item is about (its user subjects) and answers an empty page for anyone else, the same answer as an unknown identifier (RCP-01.A2 "limited to the item's subjects"). The other 13 PURP operations refuse with 403.
deviations.impact: The sweep expects 200 with no item for this operation. A-USER search in the console (AC10) is "find within this work item", not a global lookup.

deviations.deviation: admin.case_action binds its body too (not in the stage text): an explicit target must be a subject of the case, or a record whose organization or author is a subject; a revoked badge must be the target or belong to a subject organization (otherwise 403 PURPOSE_RECORD_MISMATCH and the revocation rolls back). Before, any open case let a moderator suspend, warn or penalise any account or organization. merge_duplicate's merge_into_id (the surviving organization) is not bound: it is a destination, and the merge is 4EYES.
deviations.impact: The console's badge revoke from a case works for badges of the case's organization only.

deviations.deviation: admin.media_download_url binding: a file is about itself, the records it is attached to (media_attachments) and the organization that owns it, never a system_export file through its owner. A user's own private files (vehicle photos, avatar) are reachable only through a subject record they are attached to. Verification subjects include the submitted documents.
deviations.impact: Verification documents, review evidence and files of a case target stay reachable; a user's private files are not unlocked by a case about that user (DQ-14), and DSR export bundles stay out of staff reach (S13-D1).

deviations.deviation: Subjects per kind: case = target, its author and organization (ModerationTargets handlers) and the reporters; dispute = raiser, raising organization, target and the target's parties as disputes.create checks them (review author and organization; appointment requester, requester organization and provider; badge organization; service record owner and provider; moderation action affected party and target); dsr = the requester only (RCP-01.A1 also named their organizations, the stage text did not: the narrower set was kept); verification = organization, submitter (created_by, there is no submitter column) and submitted documents; approval = the review, its author and the reviewed organization; and always the item itself. Members of a subject organization are not subjects (DQ-13).
deviations.impact: review_approval_get admits the disputed review under its dispute (the console's DisputedReview panel); review_approval_decide only under the approval item. A service-record dispute's parties depend on staff read access to vehicle_service_records; if RLS hides the row they are simply missing (fail closed), not verified with a fixture.

deviations.deviation: StaffOrgSearchRow carries, beyond the listed fields, id, slug, merged_into_organization_id and pending_verifications (id, type, created_at; at most 10) so the console can still open an organization for its pending verification (A-ORG-01 to A-ORG-02) and show a merged organization. Verification ids are not personal data. "Trust level" is trust_score (no trust-level enum exists). member_count and open_cases as before.
deviations.impact: Console: OrgHead type (search row or full view), the assign form shows the plan without the subscription status (the row has none).

deviations.deviation: suspended_until has no CHECK tying it to status = suspended: other writers (DSR deletion, first verification) change status without knowing the column, and a CHECK would make a timed-suspended user's deletion fail. stages.why_this_stage: The signed-in half of BR-19 per DQ-04. A backup key (OQ-14, R-07: two keys per staff member) makes recovery rare, and the recovery codes must exist on every account before the recovery flow (S16b) can rely on them, so this half goes first. It changes the S12 enrolment path and webauthn/mfa-service in identity, where a mistake locks staff out, so the stage is kept light. The break-glass CLI lands here so R-08 (SQL on the server) is closed even if S16b slips.

tasks.task: Docs/52 and migration: staff recovery codes (account, keyed hash, used_at, set_id, created_at). Generation per DQ-04 (10 codes, 20 Crockford base32 characters in groups of four, HMAC-SHA-256 with CARPAL_RECOVERY_CODE_PEPPER, constant-time compare, single use).

The S12 first-passkey enrolment (auth.passkey_enrol) returns the first code set once; admin.staff_me carries recovery_codes_remaining (0 for existing staff, so the console asks them to create a set); admin.staff_recovery_codes_regenerate (fresh aal3 within 5 minutes, else STEP_UP_REQUIRED; cancels the old set; returns the new set once; notice to the staff email; audited without the codes).
admin.staff_passkeys_list (own keys: label, created_at, last_used_at, device-bound, authenticator label).
admin.staff_passkey_register_options and admin.staff_passkey_register: a backup key after a fresh aal3; device-bound only (PASSKEY_NOT_DEVICE_BOUND); notice identity.staff_passkey_added.
admin.staff_passkey_remove: own key, fresh aal3, never the last key (LAST_PASSKEY); a removal notice.

Break glass: pnpm staff:break-glass --email <staff> --reason <text> (any environment, run on the server shell): disables the account's keys and sessions so the next sign-in enrols again with password + emailed code, audited as actor system with the reason, every ADM notified; deploy.md runbook section "Lost security key, fewer than two other admins".

report.note_on_order: Run at the owner's request before S15b, which is still not started (it needed DQ-19, answered the same day). S16a does not depend on S15b.
report.summary: Staff accounts now have their own recovery codes and manage their own keys on the admin plane. The first passkey enrolment (auth.passkey_enrol) returns 10 recovery codes once (AuthNext.recovery_codes); only keyed hashes are stored (identity.staff_recovery_codes, migration 0105), a code is single use and a new set voids the old one. admin.staff_me reports recovery_codes_remaining (0 for staff enrolled before S16a). Five new admin-api operations: admin.staff_passkeys_list, admin.staff_passkey_register_options, admin.staff_passkey_register, admin.staff_passkey_remove and admin.staff_recovery_codes_regenerate; the writes need a sign-in at aal3 within the last 5 minutes, synced passkeys stay refused, the last device-bound key cannot be removed (new error LAST_PASSKEY), and every change ends the other sessions and tells the account by email. Break glass: pnpm staff:break-glass (and deploy/staff-break-glass.sh) disables an account's keys and recovery codes with a reason, audited as actor system; the running backend then ends its sessions and emails the account and every other active ADM. DQ-11: disabling a staff member rejects their pending four-eyes requests in the same transaction. Every acceptance criterion is met. Also recorded: the owner's answers DQ-19 (c) and DQ-03 (documents updated; mismatches reported; DQ-20 opened).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A code set is shown once and only its keyed hashes are stored.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: s16a.int.test.ts: auth.passkey_enrol returns 10 distinct codes matching the Crockford pattern; the 10 stored rows hold 64-hex HMACs and neither form of any code; regenerate returns a new set once and its audit entries contain none of the codes.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A used code cannot be used again; regeneration voids the old set.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: s16a.int.test.ts: StaffRecoveryCodes.use accepts a code typed in lower case with spaces once, refuses it the second time, refuses another account's code and a malformed one; after a new set an unused old code is refused and a new one accepted; regenerate leaves 10 revoked rows and 10 open ones.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A backup key and regeneration need a fresh aal3.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: s16a.int.test.ts: a session that signed in 400 s ago gets 401 STEP_UP_REQUIRED with max_age=300 on regenerate, register options and remove; reading the own key list needs no step-up.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The last key cannot be removed.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: s16a.int.test.ts: with two keys one is removed (email identity.staff_passkey_removed); the last answers 409 LAST_PASSKEY; another staff member's key id answers 404.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Synced passkeys stay refused.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: s16a.int.test.ts: a synced (backup-eligible) credential answers 422 PASSKEY_NOT_DEVICE_BOUND and nothing is stored.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Break glass writes an audit entry with the reason and notifies every ADM.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: s16a.int.test.ts: breakGlassStaff refuses an unknown account and a non-staff account; for a staff account it disables 1 key and 10 codes, writes staff.break_glass as actor system with the reason and publishes staff.break_glass; the worker's relay delivers it, the account's session answers 401, the account and another ADM get their emails (the account not the ADM one), and the next sign-in enrols a key again with a new set of codes.

deviations.deviation: The keyed hash uses an HMAC key derived from the master secret (HKDF purpose staff-recovery-code, libs/crypto keys.ts) instead of a new CARPAL_RECOVERY_CODE_PEPPER variable: every other key and pepper of the backend is derived the same way (40 §2.17), and a separate variable would add a secret to back up without adding protection (whoever holds the master secret holds every key).
deviations.impact: None for clients. Replacing the master secret voids every staff recovery code (staff then create a new set).

deviations.deviation: Staff codes live in their own table (identity.staff_recovery_codes) and not as authentication_methods rows of type recovery_code: those are consumer MFA codes accepted by auth.mfa_verify and replaced by me.recovery_codes_regenerate; staff codes are never a sign-in factor. The format is XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX; input is read the Crockford way (case, spaces, hyphens, O as 0, I and L as 1).
deviations.impact: S16b uses StaffRecoveryCodes.use; consumer recovery codes are unchanged.

deviations.deviation: The caller's own key and code operations are AUD without RSN (written in the §23 intro): they change only the caller's own credentials, so the audit entry records a fixed reason instead of asking for one.
deviations.impact: The console asks for no reason on the Security keys page.

deviations.deviation: The 5-minute window is enforced by the handlers (ctx.requireAssurance('aal3', 300); the pipeline's requireAssurance gained an optional max age), and the routes also carry the AAL3 tag (10 minutes by §0.4). The STEP_UP_REQUIRED challenge says max_age=300. The older AAL3 operations (admin.case_action conditions, one §23.5 operation) still use 10 minutes although SEC-ADM-2 says 5.
deviations.impact: Console: re-authenticate when the challenge asks; aligning the older AAL3 operations to 5 minutes is listed for S25.
deviations.owner_decision: Align with SEC-ADM-2: every AAL3 admin operation uses the 5-minute window. Planned in S25a.T1 (owner, 2026-11-16)

deviations.deviation: StaffPasskey has no authenticator name: with attestation none the AAGUID is the authenticator's unverified claim and the backend keeps no AAGUID-to-model table, so the list returns the raw aaguid (null when the key gave none) and the label the staff member typed.
deviations.impact: The console names keys by their label.

deviations.deviation: Break glass ends the sessions through an outbox event (staff.break_glass, consumer identity.staff_break_glass in the running backend), because in lite mode sessions live in the server process, which a CLI cannot reach. It also voids the open recovery codes (the next enrolment issues a new set), refuses accounts without an active platform role, and also emails the account. ADMs are told by email only; the in-app staff notice comes with the staff notices of S17. A deploy wrapper deploy/staff-break-glass.sh runs it with the server environment.
deviations.impact: If the backend is stopped, the sessions end and the emails go at its next start (a restart ends every lite session anyway).

deviations.deviation: admin.staff_recovery_codes_regenerate is not IDEM (an idempotency record would keep the codes in plain text). At most 10 keys per account (409 INVALID_TRANSITION(passkey_limit)). Adding or removing a key ends the caller's other sessions (SEC-AU-4) and emails the account; regenerating emails the account. Every auth.passkey_enrol issues a set, so a re-enrolment after break glass also gets new codes.
deviations.impact: None beyond the console texts.

load.breakdown: request start and email code on the auth host 3, ADM approval queue 2.5, completion and post-recovery restriction 2.5, notices 0.5

stages.why_this_stage: The recovery flow of DQ-04 is the riskiest part of BR-19: it adds endpoints a signed-out person can call (enumeration, guessing, notification spam) and a two-approver workflow that four-eyes does not cover (four-eyes has a signed-in requester and one approver). It gets its own session so the public-endpoint protections and the state machine are built and tested with full attention.

Auth host, cp-web-admin interactions only: auth.staff_recovery_start (email, password unless password_forgotten, one recovery code) and auth.staff_recovery_verify (the emailed one-time code). The same answer and timing whatever the account state; per-account and per-IP rate limits (and the PoW of the anonymous grant where it applies); one open request per account; the recovery code is consumed when the request is created; disabled accounts never get a request. Returns an opaque request handle bound to the interaction.

Notices on creation: to the account email ("if this was not you, tell an administrator") and to every other active ADM (in-app and email; the email links to the console, nothing can be approved from it).

Admin approvals: admin.staff_recoveries_list and admin.staff_recovery_get (ADM; requester, roles, request time, IP country, password_forgotten; no codes), admin.staff_recovery_approve (fresh aal3, reason, verification_method and note; refused for the requester, for an ADM under post-recovery restriction, and twice by the same ADM) and admin.staff_recovery_reject (any ADM, reason; ends the request). Two distinct approvals move the request to approved. Also listed in admin.work_summary when S21 builds it.

Completion: auth.staff_recovery_status (by handle) and auth.staff_recovery_complete: a new password first when password_forgotten (the normal password rules), then a new device-bound key registered and proven at once (aal3). Then in one transaction: old keys, sessions and refresh tokens revoked, a new recovery-code set issued and shown once, restricted_until = now + 72 h, the account email and every ADM notified, audit entries for every step.

Post-recovery restriction: STAFF_RECOVERY_RESTRICTED on four-eyes approve, platform role grant and revoke, admin.staff_enable and admin.staff_recovery_approve while restricted_until is in the future; admin.staff_me carries restricted_until.

Tests: the full happy path (lost key, and forgotten password); no enumeration (unknown, disabled and wrong-details accounts give identical answers); rate limits; expiry at 24 h; one rejection ends the request; self-approval and double approval refused; a restricted ADM cannot approve; synced key refused at completion; sessions revoked after completion.

report.summary: A staff member who lost their security key recovers the account from the console sign-in without server access. auth.staff_recovery_start (cp-web-admin interactions only) takes the email, the password or password_forgotten, and one of the account's recovery codes; it answers 202 with an opaque handle after the same minimum time whatever the account (unknown, non-staff, disabled, wrong password or code, an open request already), and only a real request spends the code, is audited and gets an emailed code. auth.staff_recovery_verify checks that code (five wrong end it); the request then waits for approvals and every other active ADM is emailed (a link to the console only). Two different ADMs, each with a fresh aal3 (5 minutes), approve with a reason and the out-of-band check (admin.staff_recovery_approve); any ADM rejects (admin.staff_recovery_reject), also an approved request that is not completed yet; the queue is admin.staff_recoveries_list and admin.staff_recovery_get (no codes, handles or contact data). The requester polls auth.staff_recovery_status by handle and finishes on a new interaction: auth.staff_recovery_complete_options (a new password when forgotten) and auth.staff_recovery_complete (a device-bound key; synced keys refused and nothing changes). One transaction then disables the old keys and recovery codes, sets the password, issues a new code set (shown once), completes the request and restricts the account for 72 hours; every session ends, the account and every ADM are emailed, and the new key signs in at once (aal3). STAFF_RECOVERY_RESTRICTED blocks four-eyes approval, role grant and revoke, staff enable and recovery approval during the restriction; StaffMe.restricted_until shows it. Requests expire 24 hours after opening (W15 rule identity.staff_recovery_expiry; every read treats an overdue request as expired). Migration 0106. Every acceptance criterion is met.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A signed-out caller cannot tell whether an email belongs to a staff account.

deviations.deviation: The completion transaction runs when the new key's attestation is stored (auth.staff_recovery_complete); the key then proves itself at once on the same interaction through auth.webauthn_options purpose mfa and auth.mfa_verify (aal3), exactly as at the first enrolment (auth.passkey_enrol). The plan put the proof before the transaction. With attestation none, an assertion right after adds no proof of the person, and moving the recovery transaction into auth.mfa_verify would put recovery logic into every sign-in.
deviations.impact: If the browser stops between the two calls, the recovery is complete and the member signs in normally (password + new key). Console: after complete, run the usual mfa step.

deviations.deviation: The account's notice at creation is the code email itself (identity.staff_recovery_code: the code plus "if this was not you, tell an administrator"). The other ADMs are emailed when the emailed code is checked, i.e. when the request enters their queue, not at the first call: an abandoned or mistyped attempt does not alert every administrator. ADMs are told by email only; the in-app staff notice comes with the staff notices of S17 (as S16a-D6).
deviations.impact: S17: add the in-app staff notice for recovery requests and completions.

deviations.deviation: ip_country is in the table and in StaffRecoveryRequest but stays null: the backend has no IP-to-country lookup (Session.country is null for the same reason).

deviations.owner_decision: Leave empty: ip_country and Session.country stay null; a geo-IP lookup is deferred to the next phase (NP-03) (owner, 2026-11-16)

deviations.deviation: Five auth operations instead of the four named: WebAuthn needs creation options before the attestation, so completion is auth.staff_recovery_complete_options (with the new password when forgotten) then auth.staff_recovery_complete. auth.staff_recovery_status is a POST with the handle in the body (a secret kept out of URLs and logs) and needs no interaction, because the waiting page outlives the 30-minute interaction; completion runs on a new cp-web-admin interaction that presents the handle.
deviations.impact: Console BFF: keep the handle server-side (an HttpOnly cookie or the BFF session), never in browser storage (GD-12).

deviations.deviation: auth.staff_recovery_start is not tagged AUD: the pipeline requires an audit entry on every success of an AUD operation, and the dead path must answer like the live one without naming an account. Every real request is audited (staff.recovery_requested); the later steps are AUD. No proof of work: cp-web-admin is a confidential BFF client without the anonymous grant, so the PoW of the anonymous grant does not apply; the new auth.recovery bucket (3/h and 5/day per account, 10/h per IP prefix) limits it.
deviations.impact: None for clients.

deviations.deviation: expires_at holds the emailed code's 10 minutes while the request is awaiting_email_code and moves to opened + 24 hours when the code is checked, so an abandoned request blocks a new one for at most 10 minutes. admin.staff_recovery_reject also ends an approved request that is not completed yet (an administrator can stop a suspicious completion). Approvals with verification_method other need a note.
deviations.impact: Console: offer Reject on approved requests too; require the note for other.

deviations.deviation: A member disabled while a request is open is not recovered: approval answers 409 INVALID_TRANSITION(requester_disabled) and completion 409 INVALID_TRANSITION(not_approved). admin.staff_disable does not close the open request itself; it expires or an ADM rejects it.
deviations.impact: None; deploy.md says to enable a disabled member first (four eyes).

deviations.deviation: Filter meanings: city matches any active location (trimmed, case-insensitive) while the row shows the primary location's city; plan_key is the current subscription's plan, else the latest, as the row shows it; has_open_cases counts open cases about the organization itself (as open_cases); location_issue is an active far_apart pin or an open (open or triaged) wrong_location_or_closed report about the organization or any of its locations; possible_duplicate is rule-based, not the "AI flag" of Docs/23: another live organization with the same normalized name (organization.normalized_name: no case, spaces, punctuation or zero-width joiners; Arabic yeh, kaf and heh folded into Persian) and an active location in a city they share, or the same contact phone (location phones are not compared); merged and archived organizations are never flagged and never match. plan_key, has_open_cases and location_issue are answered by billing and admin through their interfaces, so the search applies them per batch of 200 organizations and looks at up to 1,000 per request: a page can hold fewer rows than limit (even none) with a next_cursor (documented in admin.orgs_search). The rows gain location_issue and possible_duplicate.

deviations.deviation: Request more info is its own entity (organization.verification_info_requests, one open request per check; 409 INVALID_TRANSITION(awaiting_business) for a second one) with fixed missing items (business_document, registration_number, legal_name, address_proof, location_pin, phone_callback, owner_identity, readable_copy, other) and templates (missing_documents, unreadable_documents, details_mismatch, location_mismatch, callback_failed, other); the console writes the message text per template, the server stores the key and the text. report.summary: Disputes can now be worked through with both parties and the trust actions of Docs/23 exist. Each dispute has two message threads, the raiser's and the other party's: staff write templated messages (the party is notified, staff names never reach it), each party reads only its own thread and answers with evidence files; the other party is recorded by the first message to it. admin.dispute_get carries a snapshot of the target (a review, the moderation action under appeal with its decider, a service record, a badge or an appointment) and the other party. Staff withdraw a dispute on the raiser's request, with the request recorded. The objection outcomes are defined by their effect in the docs (DQ-06 default). New case actions: reduce_weight keeps a review visible at a share of its weight from the next trust scoring (step-up); edit_request hides a published review until a moderator checks the author's edit (back in the queue once edited or after 7 days); downgrade_fitment lowers a fitment row's confidence. Contract 1.4.0: 458 operations, 510 routes, 55 error codes. Migration 0110. Every acceptance criterion is met.

deviations.deviation: Two threads per dispute (side raiser and respondent), not one per person: the raiser's thread serves the raising user or the raising organization's owners and managers; the respondent is the other party of the target (the review's author when the business raised it, the business when the author did; a challenged badge's provider; the other side of an appointment or service record; none for a moderation appeal). The respondent is recorded on the dispute (respondent_user_id or respondent_organization_id) by the first staff message to its side, and only then can it read and answer (RLS respondent_read, party_read, party_insert). Parties see staff as "CarPal"; a respondent never sees the raiser's statement (disputes.get stays raiser-only, now strictly the raising user). Replies carry up to 5 of the party's own clean files (purposes review_evidence, service_evidence, review_photo) attached to the message (new AttachedToType dispute_message, role evidence); staff download them under the dispute purpose (the dispute's messages are purpose subjects). At most 200 messages per thread; reply_due_at at most 30 days ahead; party replies do not notify staff (they wait in the queue).
deviations.impact: Console: A-DSP-01 thread per side (template picker, due date), the respondent from StaffDisputeDetail.respondent. PWA: dispute thread screen for both parties (follow-up); the notification already links to Activity > Reports.

deviations.deviation: The dispute purpose ends when the dispute is resolved or withdrawn (S14 queue rule), so a staff message to a closed dispute is answered 404 by the purpose check before the handler's 409 INVALID_TRANSITION(closed); a party's reply to a closed dispute is 409. Staff templates are a fixed list (DisputeMessageTemplate: request_information, request_evidence, mediation_invitation, status_update, withdrawal_confirmation, outcome_notice, other) with the text written or filled by the console; the server stores the key and the text.
deviations.impact: Console: hide Send after resolution; prefill the text per template key.

report.summary: The admin plane now serves the platform-settings and billing reads and the two dashboard aggregates the console was missing. A-PLAN-01 sees which plans are offered and which is each audience's default, lists every subscription (subscriber by public name, plan, trial end, expiry, overrides, who assigned it; trials ending soon) and works the organizations' plan requests as a queue. A-RET-01 adds a policy with a second administrator and runs a dry run that counts, per status, what the next daily run would delete or anonymize (also previewing another period or status) without changing anything. Feature flags and exchange rates carry their audit ids, so their history opens. The dashboard gets admin.system_health (failed imports, deliveries and virus scans in 24 h, 7 days and 30 days, with the last failure) and admin.work_summary: per queue the caller's roles may list, the open count, the caller's share, the oldest item, the next target, items per SLA state (with paused verifications) and a breakdown by status, source, reason, type or severity, so My work no longer pages every list each minute. Contract 1.4.0: 469 operations, 521 routes, 55 error codes. Migration 0112 (two partial indexes). Every acceptance criterion is met.

report.summary: An organization merge now moves the business's records to the surviving organization instead of only marking the duplicate. report.summary: The admin console can now fill the user and organization tabs that only had placeholders. On a user (A-USR-02): the vehicles the user owns with brand, model, year and status (the VIN shows its last four characters, the plate its last two, documents and notes are never read); the appointments the user requested with the business, vehicle, type, status and dates (never the description or contact data); the full consent history, read-only; and the active sessions and push devices (never a token). On an organization (A-ORG-02): the capability matrix and every badge with the rule evaluation that awarded it; the showcases with consent status, the customer's consent record by display name and open cases; the inventory quality (counts, data quality, confirmed fitment, inquiry fulfillment, the catalog quality score computed now and the flagged items); the members and pending invitations; and the plan history with who assigned each plan and the plan request it answered. Every read needs a purpose naming a work item about that user or organization (403 PURPOSE_RECORD_MISMATCH otherwise, S14); the six reads with personal data write a pii.read audit entry naming the case and the subject. Contract 1.4.0: 479 operations, 531 routes, 55 error codes. No migration. Every acceptance criterion is met.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every read is PURP and bound per S14.

The generated sweep suites (vehicle, appointment, identity, organization, inventory, billing) run each new route with a resolver whose check asserts the masked plate, no description, no token, the badge and consent blocks, and the dynamic projection scan.

report.summary: Users and businesses can now ask CarPal for help inside the apps, and staff have an inbox for it. A user files a ticket (topic, subject, description, app area, optional diagnostic info, and the business when they act for one), sees only their own tickets, reads CarPal's answers (staff shown as "CarPal") and replies; a reply within 14 days reopens a solved ticket; at most 5 open tickets per user. There is no email intake (DQ-07). Staff (support and admins) list the inbox with the team's clock (first response within 1 working day, paused while waiting on the user), read a ticket only under its purpose ticket:<id> (subjects: the requester and the business; moderators and community reviewers never), assign it, answer with templates, turn it into a moderation case (the user's report, triaged into the target's open case or a new one with the severity floor), a privacy request, a dispute or a plan request (DQ-20 row 4, confirmed), and close it with an outcome; every staff action needs a reason and is audited with the purpose. The user is notified of each staff answer and of the solved ticket (support_update: in the app, plus an email or push notice that points to the app). The work summary has a support_tickets queue; a deletion request erases the tickets, an export includes them, and retention can purge solved tickets. Contract 1.4.0: 489 operations, 541 routes, 55 error codes. Migration 0114. Every acceptance criterion is met. BR-14 (AI review decisions) is deferred to the next phase by the owner.

report.summary: The owner's decisions of 2026-11-16 are built. Staff re-authenticate within 5 minutes for every AAL3 action on the admin plane (four-eyes decisions, the heavy case actions, recovery approval, own keys), as SEC-ADM-2 says; consumers keep 10 minutes. The notification rules now hold the reminders to businesses about reviews waiting for their approval (default days 3 and 6, sent by a new sweep), and how early maintenance reminders become due by date and by mileage (default 14 days and 500 km, the old code values; the vehicle sweep follows them). Administrators get a Delivery health read: attempts, failures and the failure rate per channel and provider over 24 hours, 7 and 30 days. A rejected verification now tells the owners and managers what to fix. The author of hidden or removed content is recorded on the moderation action and can appeal it. An upheld dispute that would remove a review or revoke a badge no longer applies at once: it waits for a different administrator's fairness approval, and the content stays until then. Support tickets left waiting on the user for 7 days are closed as no_response by the system. Contract 1.4.0: 490 operations, 542 routes, 55 error codes. Migration 0115. Every acceptance criterion is met.

deviations.deviation: The window lives in the Authenticator: a staff principal's step-up defaults to 300 s (ADMIN_STEP_UP_MAX_AGE_S) and a caller may only shorten it, so every AAL3 check on the admin plane uses 5 minutes: the AAL3 tag (admin.four_eyes_decide, admin.staff_recovery_approve, the five staff key and code operations), the conditional AAL3 of admin.case_action (suspend_account, apply_trust_penalty, merge_duplicate, reduce_weight) and the admin-host challenge for a non-aal3 session. The "§23.5 operation" of the plan is admin.four_eyes_decide. Consumer step-up keeps 10 minutes.
deviations.impact: Console (AC14): re-authenticate when a challenge says max_age=300; a step-up older than 5 minutes no longer passes four-eyes decisions or the heavy case actions.

deviations.deviation: The maintenance and mileage "reminder cadence" of Docs/23 is read, as the plan says, as the due windows the vehicle code had hard-coded: a maintenance reminder becomes due 14 days before its date or 500 km before its mileage (now NotificationRules.maintenance_due_window_days 1-90 and mileage_due_window_km 50-5000). The hourly vehicle sweep applies them and never takes a due reminder back to upcoming when the window narrows. reminders.create / reminders.update and AI-suggested reminders still compute their first status with the default window, because the api role cannot read notification_rules (S17 grant); the sweep corrects it within the hour. Docs/21 also lists a "Monthly mileage reminder" (a prompt to update the odometer, C-GARAGE-08): the backend has no such reminder and S25a does not add one.
deviations.impact: Owner: say whether the monthly odometer prompt is wanted (a new rule, event and template, about 2 points); it is not in deferred_to_next_phase yet.

deviations.deviation: Path 2 approval reminders: a new 15-minute sweep trust.approval_reminders sends review.approval.reminded for a review still pending_approval with business_confirmation_status pending on each day of NotificationRules.review_approval_reminder_days (0-3 days, each 1-6, default 3 and 6). The request time is business_confirmation_due_at minus the 7-day window (also right for reviews staff moved to Path 2). trust.reviews.business_reminder_count keeps the reminders sent; a day missed while the sweep was down is not sent twice (the count jumps to the latest day reached). The notice reuses the review_approval_needed event type with the new template review.approval_reminder (days_left); review.approval.reminded is a worker event like review.invitation.reminded and is not listed in Appendix A.
deviations.impact: PWA / business portal: classify review.approval_reminder as a business template (done in BUSINESS_TEMPLATE_KEYS); the link is the review approval page.

deviations.deviation: Delivery health is a new admin.notif_delivery_health (STF(ADM): A-NOTIF-01 is an administrator screen). The sender ports name their provider (optional Mailer/SmsSender/PushSender.provider: file in lite mode, smtp, sms_gateway, push_gateway in full mode) and the dispatcher stores it on each attempt (notification_deliveries.provider; digests too); deliveries attempted before S25a show provider unknown. A delivery counts once, in its last state (sent, delivered or failed) at the time of its last attempt (updated_at): a failure retried successfully counts as sent. Every channel (email, push, SMS) is listed, with the current sender's provider when it had no attempt. Aggregates only, no recipients or error texts.

deviations.deviation: A rejected check publishes organization.verification.rejected (organization, check id, type and rejection_reason, never the reviewer); the owners and managers (ORG_ADMINS) get organization.verification_rejected in the app, by email and by push. The email and the in-app params carry rejection_reason, the text written for the business (OrganizationVerification.rejection_reason, which the business already reads); the push text is short and names no reason. There is no separate reason category: VerificationDecision has only rejection_reason.

deviations.deviation: admin.case_action records the author as params.user_id on every content action (approve, hide, remove, restore, request_changes) and on the target actions (reduce_weight, edit_request, apply_redaction, downgrade_fitment) when the target has an author, so admin.moderation_action_affects names the author and disputes.create accepts the author's moderation_appeal. The subject organization keeps its route (subject_organization_id). Backfill: none. deviations.deviation: Removal outcomes, confirmed from outcomeAction: remove (fake_review upheld) and revoke_badge (badge_challenge upheld). admin.dispute_resolve then answers 202 PendingChange (op admin.dispute_resolve, target the dispute, required role platform_admin), applies nothing, assigns the dispute to the resolver when it had no assignee and writes dispute.resolution_requested; a second request while one is pending is 409 DUPLICATE. StaffDispute.pending_change_id shows "Awaiting administrator approval" (FourEyes.pendingFor). The executor runs in the approver's transaction: the dispute must still be open, the approver must not be the raiser, the first reviewer or the author of the disputed moderation action, and the resolution is applied with the resolver as resolved_by and the approver recorded in the moderation action (params.approved_by) and the audit entry. While a removal waits, the resolver can still move the dispute to mediation or reject the claim (both apply at once); the pending change then fails with 409 INVALID_TRANSITION when approved, and is rejected or expires.
deviations.impact: Console (AC14): A-DSP-01 handles 202 (show "Awaiting administrator approval", disable Uphold while pending_change_id is set); Pending approvals lists the change for administrators only. Breaking for the console only (contract row in Appendix D).

tasks.task: Pilot administrators with a forced password change. (a) Seed: deploy/templates/staff-bootstrap.json.example lists admin100, admin200, admin300 (ADM, DQ-26 addresses) as the three main administrators, keeping the backup ADM, MOD and CRV entries for the owner to fill; staff:bootstrap uses CARPAL_STAFF_INITIAL_PASSWORD (backend.env; empty by default; never printed or logged) as the initial password of every account it creates, and the generated one-time password as today when it is empty. The initial password is exempt from SEC-AU-7 only under DQ-25's limits; dev keeps DEV_STAFF_PASSWORD. (b) Every account created with an initial or one-time password is marked password_change_required, with initial_password_expires_at = created + 7 days (DQ-25). (c) Sign-in on cp-web-admin: password -> the code sent to the account email (the enrolment code, also asked of an account that already has a key when the flag is set) -> new interaction step change_password: new operation auth.password_set_initial on the auth host (new password twice; SEC-AU-7 length and breached check; must differ from the initial password; rate-limited like auth.signin) -> passkey enrolment or WebAuthn -> aal3. No token is issued while the flag is set. The emailed code comes before the change, so knowing the shared initial password is not enough to take an account over. After the expiry the initial password is refused with the generic sign-in error, and a new one is set from the server shell (staff:bootstrap --reissue <email>, audited, dev and staging and prod). (d) Audit staff.initial_password_changed; email identity.password_changed; security log event. (e) Existing staff that already signed in are unchanged. Tests: the step order, no token before the change, a weak or equal new password refused, the flag cleared once, expiry, reissue, the code wrong five times ends the interaction.

Email through the carpals.ir mailbox (meta.email_check_2026_11_16). (a) A real SMTP Mailer (nodemailer, pooled, timeouts 10/20/30 s) replaces the full-mode skeleton and can also be chosen in lite mode: CARPAL_MAIL_TRANSPORT = file (default in dev and tests) | smtp; CARPAL_SMTP_URL = smtps://<user>:<password>@mail.carpals.ir:465 (implicit TLS; or smtp://...:587 with STARTTLS required, never plain), CARPAL_MAIL_FROM (default "CarPal <no-reply@carpals.ir>"), optional CARPAL_MAIL_REPLY_TO. Staging and prod refuse transport smtp without TLS and refuse a certificate that does not verify. (b) Multipart text + the existing plain-text body (HTML only if the templates already render it), Persian subjects encoded correctly, Message-ID on the sending domain, List-Unsubscribe only on optional mail. (c) Failures map to the dispatcher's retry classes (4xx / connection errors retry, 5xx permanent), and provider "smtp" is recorded per attempt (Delivery health). (d) A send cap per hour (CARPAL_MAIL_MAX_PER_HOUR, default 300) protects the shared hosting quota: above it, non-critical mail waits; sign-in codes and security notices go first. (e) deploy.md: create the mailbox in cPanel, the settings, a test from the API server (openssl s_client -connect mail.carpals.ir:465 and pnpm mail:test --to <address>), SPF/DKIM/DMARC notes, the hourly cap to confirm with the host. Tests: against a local SMTP test server (TLS, auth, a 4xx retry, a 5xx failure, the hourly cap order).

tasks.task: SMS gateway module with a mock provider. (a) A port SmsGateway in libs/sms (used by the existing SmsSender path and the OTP code): sendText(to, text, {category, idempotencyKey}) -> {provider_message_id, status, segments}; sendOtp(to, code, {templateKey, locale}) (the template or "lookup" style most Iranian SMS APIs offer for verification codes, with sendText as the fallback); status(providerMessageId) -> queued | sent | delivered | failed | unknown; balance() -> credit or null; plus helpers every provider shares: E.164 check against region sms_country_codes (+98), segment count (GSM-7 160/153, Unicode/Persian 70/67), opt-out keywords. (b) Provider registry selected by CARPAL_SMS_PROVIDER = mock (default) | file (the old sink) | <vendor> later; vendor keys reserved in .env.example (CARPAL_SMS_API_KEY, CARPAL_SMS_SENDER_LINE, CARPAL_SMS_OTP_TEMPLATE) and a documented adapter skeleton, so adding the chosen provider is one adapter file and its tests. (c) Mock provider: behaves like a real one without sending anything: returns message ids, writes each message to outbox-sms.jsonl (codes included, file readable by root only outside dev), moves status to delivered after a configurable delay, fails on purpose for configured test numbers (permanent and temporary) so retries and Delivery health can be tested, reports a fake balance. (d) Delivery status: a sweep polls status() for sent messages for up to 24 h and records delivered/failed on the delivery row (Delivery health counts it). (e) Outside dev the mock is allowed (owner decision) but the startup log warns every hour that no SMS leaves the server, and admin.system_health shows sms_provider = mock (DQ-28). Tests: the port contract run against the mock (and later each vendor adapter), segments, E.164, failures and retries, status sweep.

IRR rate set every morning. (a) Default from configuration: CARPAL_DEFAULT_IRR_PER_USD (decimal string, default 1000000; .env.example, deploy/templates/backend.env.template, README). At start the backend inserts the region's display-currency row with this value when it is missing (reason "default from configuration", audited as system); it never overwrites a rate an administrator set. config.client therefore always serves an IRR rate. (b) Freshness: the admin ExchangeRate view gains set_today (updated since 00:00 in the region time zone, Asia/Tehran) and age_hours. (c) Morning reminder: a sweep admin.exchange_rate_reminder sends a staff notice (console in-app and email) to active ADMs at CARPAL_RATE_REMINDER_HOUR (default 9, region time) when the rate was not set that day, once per day, linking to the Exchange rates page; no notice once it is set. (d) Unchanged: four eyes for a change over 20 % (rateNeedsSecondApprover); the reason is still required; clients see a change within five minutes. Record in deploy.md that a daily move over 20 % (a sharp devaluation) waits for a second ADM. Tests: missing row created from the setting, an existing row untouched, set_today across midnight Tehran time, one reminder per day, none after the rate is set.

Consent-text seed. New command pnpm seed:consent-texts --file <json> [--region ir-pilot] (tools/db; runs on the server like staff:bootstrap, deploy/seed-consent-texts.sh). It validates the file against the template shape (database/seeds/consent-texts.template.json): all 13 consent types once, title and body in EN and FA, Markdown without HTML, no [bracketed] placeholder left (allowed only with --allow-placeholders in dev), meta.status approved. It creates each text as a DRAFT version (policy_version from the file, 1.1 in the template) of the consent type's document in the region, as actor system with an audit entry; a type that already has that version is reported and left alone; published versions are never changed. Publishing stays in the console (A-POL-01, admin.policy_version_publish, four eyes, effective date, requires_reconsent from the file). Tests: a valid file creates 13 drafts, a second run creates none, placeholders refused outside dev, HTML refused, a missing type refused.

deviations.deviation: auth.password_set_initial (POST /v1/auth/password/initial) takes the emailed code and the new password in one call. The code check counts toward the same five attempts as the enrolment code; the fifth wrong code ends the interaction (410 LINK_EXPIRED afterwards). tasks.task: Monthly odometer prompt (voluntary). (a) Rule: NotificationRules.odometer_prompt_days, default 30, 0 = off, otherwise 14-90 (admin.notif_rules_get/update, If-Match; A-NOTIF-01 Rules). (b) A daily sweep vehicle.odometer_prompts at the rules' digest_hour in the region time zone: for every active personal vehicle (DQ-27) whose newest reading (by recorded_at; the vehicle's created_at when it has none) is older than odometer_prompt_days, and that was not prompted or skipped in the current cycle, publish vehicle.odometer_prompt.due -> template vehicle.odometer_prompt to the owner (in app and push; email off by default; category reminders, so the person can switch it off in notification preferences; quiet hours respected), reference the vehicle, deep link C-GARAGE-08. One prompt per vehicle per cycle; an ignored prompt is not repeated until the next cycle. (c) Skip: new operation vehicles.odometer_prompt_skip (POST, the vehicle owner, no body, idempotent within the cycle) records the skip, writes no reading, marks the in-app notice done and moves the next prompt one interval ahead; analytics event odometer_prompt.skipped (vehicle id only). (d) Answer: any vehicles.mileage_add whose recorded_at is the newest reading ends the cycle (the next prompt is due odometer_prompt_days after it); analytics odometer_prompt.answered when the reading arrives while a prompt is open. (e) Vehicle view: odometer_prompt { due: boolean, due_since: datetime|null } so the PWA can show a garage card without push. (f) Historical order (owner: "record data in historical sequence"): confirm and test that vehicles.mileage_add stores recorded_at as given (back-dated readings allowed, at most 5 minutes in the future), vehicles.mileage_list returns readings newest first by recorded_at, Vehicle.mileage_km mirrors the newest reading by recorded_at (not the newest insert), lower_than_previous is judged against the reading before it in time, and a back-dated reading does not end the current cycle. Tests: due after 30 days, not due after a reading, skip moves the cycle, off at 0, ignored prompt not repeated, sold/inactive vehicles skipped, back-dated insert order.

NeshanGeocoder implements the Geocoder port (search, reverse, locate) server-side with the Neshan service key (CARPAL_NESHAN_SERVICE_KEY in backend.env, never sent to clients; CARPAL_GEOCODER = fixture (dev and tests) | neshan | unconfigured). First confirm from the docs the endpoints and versions; as known before the docs went down (to be verified, not taken as fact): base https://api.neshan.org, header Api-Key: <service key>, search GET /v1/search?term=&lat=&lng= (results near a point; use the city centre or the map centre the caller gives), geocoding GET /v4/geocoding?address= (or a newer version), reverse GET /v5/reverse?lat=&lng=. Map the answers to GeocodeCandidate (label, point, address_line_1, city, region, postal_code null when absent, country IR) and validate them like client input (SEC-IN-10). Timeouts (3 s), a circuit breaker and 503 UNAVAILABLE with retry-after on provider failure, so the location editor keeps working by typed address; results cached in KV for 24 h per normalized query (confirm the terms allow it); no consumer search-as-you-type through this port (Plan §2 rule kept: the clients call geo.* on submit or with a debounce of at least 500 ms and 3 characters). Usage counters per day for the owner (quota and cost), visible in admin.system_health. Tests: adapter against recorded Neshan answers (fixtures), errors, timeouts, cache, the pin-versus-address check with Neshan results.
tasks.neshan_findings_2026_11_16: Docs site down (HTTP 503 from Neshan's CDN). From Neshan's own npm package @neshan-maps-platform/mapbox-gl 1.1.5 (read as data, not run): the web SDK is a fork of mapbox-gl 1.13.2 and needs a "web map" key (mapKey); its vector styles (neshanVector, neshanVectorNight; raster variants exist) use tiles from https://vts.neshan.org/basemap/v2/{z}/{x}/{y}/platform and https://vts.neshan.org/poi/v3/{z}/{x}/{y}/platform, traffic from https://tvts.neshan.org/traffic/v4/..., sprites https://static.neshan.org/sdk/mapboxgl/sprites/sprite, glyphs https://static.neshan.org/sdk/mapboxgl/fontstack/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf, the RTL text plugin https://static.neshan.org/sdk/mapboxgl/mapbox-gl-rtl-text.js, raster hosts tile1-8.neshan.org, and an attribution/watermark linking platform.neshan.org. The SDK stores the key in localStorage (which the console's GD-12 rule forbids), and how the key is attached to tile requests is obfuscated in the bundle: confirm from the docs before choosing between MapLibre with a Neshan style (preferred: keeps the existing map code and CSP) and Neshan's SDK.

tasks.task: Map configuration for Neshan. The SDK maps nsh:// to https with ?key=<apiKey> in the query and XOR-decodes then gunzips each tile with a table built into the SDK, so plain maplibre-gl cannot read the tiles; it also builds its worker from a blob URL (createObjectURL + importScripts), which a CSP with worker-src 'self' and Trusted Types refuses. The logo and copyright may be moved, not hidden; tiles need DecompressionStream (Chrome 80+, Firefox 113+, Safari 16.4+). Neshan offers raster tiles to verified companies on request (panel ticket). The admin console chose option (c) on the owner's decision (console OQ-16): no basemap, an "Open in Neshan" link per location (RegionConfig.navigation_apps). deviations.deviation: SEC-WEB-3 "CSRF token" on the auth host is the interaction binding that exists since S11: the __Host-cp_ia cookie must name the body's interaction_id (required in strict mode, which staging and prod run). No new synchronizer token and no token-read operation; the routes without an interaction (password reset, email verification, staff recovery) carry no cookie and so no ambient authority. The Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site checks run in every mode. Recorded in Docs/40 §6.2.
deviations.why: A new required header would break the PWA and console /id proxies until they change; the existing binding already defeats cross-site use of the only cookie the auth host reads.

deviations.deviation: The forwarded client IP is its own signed header, CarPal-Forwarded-Client (compact JWS with the client's private_key_jwt key, typ carpal-fwd+jwt, aud = host URL, htm/htu bound like DPoP, at most 60 s, no single-use jti), not the /oauth/token client assertion, which exists only at the token endpoint. A statement that does not verify is ignored and logged (security_event forwarded_client_refused), never refused, and it is accepted from any peer (the signature is the trust), unlike X-Forwarded-For.
deviations.why: API and /id calls carry no client assertion; refusing a bad statement would let a BFF bug lock every web user out.

deviations.deviation: NI-19 is partly done: the backend accepts the BFF header, but the PWA and console BFFs do not send it yet, so web calls still count against 127.0.0.1. The raised IP windows stay in the backend.env template (CARPAL_RATE_LIMITS) and deploy.md Known limitation 3 is reworded instead of removed. Hand-offs: pwa/BR-update-plan.json PB-12, console AC14b.T7.
deviations.why: BFF code is outside the backend plan.

deviations.deviation: PoW (NI-19 d): a per-client difficulty setting, CARPAL_POW_CLIENT_DIFFICULTY_BITS, that is empty by default (nothing is lowered silently); the up-front solving in strict mode is PWA work (PB-12). CarPal-Client is declared by the caller, so a lower web value applies to anyone who names that client (deploy template note).
deviations.why: The difficulty is a security trade-off for the owner and the PWA, not a backend default.

deviations.deviation: Raw uploads are encrypted at rest in every environment, dev included (signed PUT stores them encrypted; get() decrypts for W6). The one-time migration runs at backend start, not as a separate command: idempotent, the file state is decided by its bytes against the sidecar SHA-256 (a run cut short is finished by the next), writes go to a temporary file and are renamed. A plaintext file left afterwards refuses the start; pnpm preflight reports the count before an update.
deviations.why: One code path for every environment; the operator has nothing to remember.

deviations.deviation: NI-18 (e) goes further than the master secret: the development login-role passwords (<role>_dev, the defaults) are refused outside dev too, each naming its CARPAL_DB_PASSWORD_* key. Keys derived from the development master secret need that secret, which is refused, so they are not checked separately. Master-secret rotation (re-encryption of stored media) is not built; deploy.md says to rotate only after a compromise.
deviations.why: The role passwords are public in the code like the master secret.

deviations.deviation: The one-process rule (NI-18 d) is a lock file with the owner's pid (/carpal/data/backend.lock), not a PostgreSQL advisory lock. The lock records the pid, the boot id and the entry script; a lock from an earlier boot, whose pid is gone, or (Linux) whose pid now runs another program (for example the PWA's node process after a reboot reused the pid) is taken over, so a crash or reboot does not block the restart. The separate deployables (apps/api, auth, admin-api, worker) take the same lock in lite mode outside dev; dev is not locked.
deviations.why: The lite data folder, not the database, is what a second process would corrupt; the lock must also survive a lost connection.

decisions_needed.question: Lost-key reset design (your research on the 2026-11-09 risk review): ADM reset with four-eyes and re-enrolment by password + emailed code, or something stronger (e.g. an in-person check, a waiting period)?
decisions_needed.default: As in BR-19 raw_text.
decisions_needed.answer: Recommended process approved (owner, 2026-11-13), replacing both the default (ADM-initiated reset with four-eyes) and the owner's first proposal (requester names two approvers, approvers type 128-character paper codes through an emailed 10-minute link).

decision.recovery_codes: Every staff account holds its own 10 single-use recovery codes: 20 characters each from Crockford base32 (no ambiguous characters, no symbols, so they can be typed on any keyboard layout), shown in groups of four (about 100 bits). Shown once when the first passkey is enrolled (and to existing staff at their next sign-in), written or printed by the staff member, stored sealed and apart from the security keys. Stored as keyed hashes (HMAC-SHA-256 with a server pepper), compared in constant time. Can be replaced after a fresh aal3 sign-in; the new set cancels the old sheet.
decision.requester_proof: Lost key: email + password + one of the account's own recovery codes + a one-time code sent to the staff email. Forgotten password as well: email + recovery code + emailed code, and the requester sets a new password at the end. The requester never names approvers. The answer is the same whether or not the account exists, is disabled or the details are wrong; attempts are rate-limited per account and per IP; one open request per account; disabled accounts cannot recover.
decision.notification: Creating a request notifies the account's email ("a recovery was requested for your account; if this was not you, tell an administrator") and every other active ADM (in-app and email). The email only links to the console; no approval is possible from a link.
decision.approvals: Two different ADMs, neither the requester, each signed in to the console with their passkey and a fresh aal3 (within 5 minutes), approve with a reason and the out-of-band check they made (call to a known number, in person, video call, other + note). Any one ADM can reject, which ends the request. Approvers under post-recovery restriction cannot approve. The whole request expires after 24 hours.
decision.completion: After two approvals the requester (same browser, holding the request handle) registers a new device-bound key (security key or Windows Hello; synced passkeys refused with PASSKEY_NOT_DEVICE_BOUND) and proves it at once (aal3). The password stays unless the request said it was forgotten. Then: old keys and all sessions and refresh tokens revoked, a new recovery-code set issued (the old sheet is void), the account email and every ADM notified, everything audited.
decision.restriction_after_recovery: For 72 hours the recovered account cannot approve four-eyes changes, grant or revoke roles, enable staff, or approve another recovery (STAFF_RECOVERY_RESTRICTED).
decision.roles: The same flow for every staff role (ADM, MOD, CRV, SUP), always with two ADM approvers (see DQ-15).
decision.break_glass: When fewer than two other ADMs are active, a documented server procedure (a staff CLI run on the server shell, with a reason, audited as actor system, all ADMs notified) disables the account's keys so the next sign-in enrols again. This replaces the "SQL on the server" fallback of R-08.
decision.replaces: The planned admin.staff_passkeys_reset (ADM resets another member's keys with four-eyes) is dropped: a suspected compromise is handled by admin.staff_disable (S13), and the member comes back through recovery after re-enabling (4EYES, DQ-10).

decisions_needed.question: The owner wrote "appeals can not auto-remove before fairness approve by admin". Today an upheld dispute applies its outcome at once (an upheld fake_review removes the review; an upheld badge_challenge revokes the badge; an upheld moderation_appeal restores the content). Which rule is meant?
options: Removal waits for ADM: when an upheld dispute or appeal would remove content, the removal waits for an ADM fairness approval (four eyes) and the content stays up until then.
No automatic close or purge while an appeal is open.
decisions_needed.answer: Removal waits for ADM (owner, 2026-11-16): an upheld dispute or appeal whose outcome removes something from public view does not apply at resolution; a different administrator (ADM, not a moderator) approves it as fair through four eyes, and until then the content stays as it is. Outcomes that restore or change nothing apply at once, as today.

decisions_needed.question: The chosen initial password has 9 characters. SEC-AU-7 asks for at least 12, and a keyboard pattern like this one is likely to be in breached-password lists. Should the seed accept it anyway, as a one-time password that must be changed at the first sign-in?
decisions_needed.default: Yes, with limits: the initial password is accepted only by the staff seed, only for accounts that have never signed in, only together with the code sent to the account email, and only for 7 days after the account is created (then the account needs a new initial password from the server shell). The new password chosen at the first sign-in must meet SEC-AU-7 (12+ characters, not breached, not the initial one). The value lives in backend.env, never in git.
decisions_needed.risk: Anyone who learns the shared initial password still needs the account mailbox to get past the emailed code, and the code comes before the password change, so the password alone cannot take over an account.

S26a is built and tested (contract 1.5.0 opened). Staff accounts seeded with the owner's initial password (CARPAL_STAFF_INITIAL_PASSWORD, never printed or committed) must enter the code sent to their email and choose a new 12+ character password before their key; no token is issued before that, and the initial password expires after 7 days (staff:bootstrap --reissue). Email goes through the carpals.ir cPanel mailbox by authenticated SMTP (CARPAL_MAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp, TLS required, hourly cap, 4xx retried, 5xx permanent, provider smtp in Delivery health); pnpm mail:test and deploy/email_setup_guide.md cover the setup. Every SMS goes through the new SmsGateway port; the mock provider gives ids, statuses, failures and a balance, a sweep records delivered/failed, System health and config.client say SMS is simulated, and the log warns hourly outside dev. The IRR rate is never blank (created from CARPAL_DEFAULT_IRR_PER_USD when missing), ExchangeRate has set_today and age_hours, and administrators get one morning reminder on days the rate was not set. pnpm seed:consent-texts loads the 13 reviewed texts as drafts. DQ-25, DQ-26 and DQ-28 were built on their defaults and wait for the owner's confirmation. Contract 1.5.0: 491 operations, 543 routes (490 served), 55 error codes. Migration 0116.

T0 (BR-36, BR-37, done 2026-11-18, commit b93f5c1): verification queue page in batched reads, q organization_id and verification_id. T1 (NI-18): outside dev the backend refuses to start with PostgreSQL fsync, synchronous_commit or full_page_writes off, the development master secret or a <role>_dev role password, or a missing or http CARPAL_MEDIA_BASE_URL (the DI-26 https rewrite runs in dev only); raw uploads are encrypted at rest from the signed PUT on, and plaintext ones stored earlier are encrypted once at start; a second lite backend process against the same data refuses to start (backend.lock); each refusal names its setting, and deploy/2-build.sh runs the same checks as pnpm preflight before the restart. T2 (NI-19, backend half): POST /v1/auth/* refuses cross-site browser requests (Sec-Fetch-Site, Origin against the issuer and CARPAL_AUTH_WEB_ORIGINS; 403 CSRF_FAILED); X-Forwarded-For is trusted from CARPAL_TRUSTED_PROXIES only (the last address that is not a proxy); a BFF can state its visitor's address in the signed header CarPal-Forwarded-Client; cp-ssr without it uses ssr.read and ssr.search, with it the normal buckets per visitor; taxonomy.suggest has its own bucket RL(typeahead); PoW difficulty can be set per client (not set by default). T3: contract frozen, deploy kit (template keys, preflight, key check, deploy.md: one process, startup checks, key rotation, client addresses, migrations 0116-0117 = 18 applied), NI items updated, hand-offs PB-12 and AC14b.T7/T8.
